summary: Richibucto Head light at Cap-Lumière, New Brunswick: lit 2 May 1865, kept until 1965 when it was electrified, still an active Coast Guard light.

lens.note: Fourth-order lens for the inaugural lighting on 2 May 1865 (Lighthouse Friends). The sources do not describe the current optic.

structures.type: square pyramidal wood tower with lantern and gallery
structures.note: Built to a contract of 1863: quadrangular wooden tower on a masonry foundation 16 ft square at the base (Lighthouse Friends). CCG List of Lights gives 10.5 m structure height above ground, white square tower with red upper portion. Rowlett gives 9 m (30 ft), painted white with red trim.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed. On Cap Lumière Road off Route 505 (Rowlett).

events.note: House of Assembly of New Brunswick authorised a lighthouse on Richibucto Head at a cost of £250; work did not begin
John Wilkinson examined the coast in May 1861 and preferred a sandy point four miles south-east of the harbour entrance; the light was built a short distance south of it, on Richibucto Head
Amos Keith contracted at $592 to build the tower by 1 July 1863
Inaugural lighting on 2 May 1865 with the fourth-order lens
Tower reshingled and painted after leaks in rainstorms; new lantern deck
Round wick lamp replaced the flat wick lamp
Light electrified; Fred Joseph Blanchard, the final keeper, left in 1965 (Lighthouse Friends)

corrections.why: The 1901 change in the Department's report concerns the south-beach range lights (cite 3). The Head is still in the Department's 1906 keeper list and 1913 statement (cites 5, 6), and the CCG list shows the light active (cite 2). Lighthouse Friends gives 1865 as the first lighting and says the light remains active (cite 1).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikidata gives inactive. The CCG List of Lights (Fl W 5s, year round), Rowlett ('Active') and Lighthouse Friends ('remains active') all give an active light. The record's active status stands.
Lighthouse Friends gives the inaugural lighting as 2 May 1865, and Rowlett's directory gives 1865. A tourism listing gives 1864 and a 1988 alteration; it cites no source and is not used.
The Coast Guard's List of Lights calls the station Richibucto Cape; Rowlett and Lighthouse Friends use Richibucto Head (Cap Lumière). Both names are kept.
Rowlett gives 9 m (30 ft) for the tower; the CCG list gives a 10.5 m structure height above ground. The record's 10.0 m sits between them and is not changed.

notes_for_editor: Sources: the keeper roster and the 1857-1870 history come from Lighthouse Friends alone; the Department reports for those years are not in the local corpus (the corpus begins in fiscal 1900). Lighthouse Friends is copyrighted: the story paraphrases it and quotes only short phrases. Fabien (Robicheau) Richard: the roster starts him in 1864, but the first lighting was 2 May 1865; the story keeps the roster's date and says so. Peter F. Richard: the 1906 list row 'Richard, Peter F ... Richibuctou Head' was checked on the page image on 2026-10-28 (printed p. 171, scan 180): the name, station and appointment date (May 30, 1895) share a row, and the OCR name and station blocks each run to 24 entries in the same order. The 1901 range-light dates (1 August and 8 October 1901) are given in the story by date, because they fall after the fiscal year ended 30 June 1901 that the report is labelled with; the report's Chief Engineer section does not mention the Head. The 1909 keeper table prints 'Peter F. Richard' followed by 'May 30, 1895' in column-split OCR; it is not matched to the station, but 1895 agrees with Lighthouse Friends. The 1902 list line 'Richard, Peter F Richibucto' gives the station as just 'Richibucto', which could be the Head, a range or the beach light, so it is not used. The 1903 and 1904 lists print 'Richibuctou Head' with no keeper on the same line, and the 1913 statement prints 'Richibucto head' in a separate column from the names; neither is matched. The 1912 'bungalow at station, Richibucto' and 1913 'Richibucto. - Station in commission from April to November' refer to a life-saving station in the town, not this light. No wreck or rescue tied to the Head was found, so the story has no storms chapter. Wikidata's 1901 first_lit and deactivated events are not supported (see corrections). The Wikipedia article for this light returned 404 and was not used. The tourism listing (1864; 1988 alteration) is unsourced and was not used. The Parks Canada and CRHP searches found no designation record for this light, and no designation is claimed. No Canadian newspaper archive was reachable. The Lighthouse Friends roster spells Maxime P. Richard twice (1934-35 and 1944-47); both are kept.
